extracted.intended_audience: researchers, authors, and readers who post or moderate comments on PubPeer (post-publication peer reviewers)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and standards for writing, posting, and moderating post-publication peer review comments on the PubPeer platform. Covers what to say, how to support claims, anonymity, moderation, and legal/ethical limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose of PubPeer / scope of commentary
rubrics_metrics.description: PubPeer is a forum for post-publication peer review: to discuss, critique, and improve the scientific literature by allowing readers to comment on published articles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments should address the published research itself (data, methods, figures, claims, reproducibility), not unrelated personal matters. Use the platform to point out errors, inconsistencies, replication attempts, or other science-relevant observations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be specific about what you are commenting on
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify the exact location in the paper that your comment concerns (e.g., figure and panel number, table, page, paragraph, or specific sentence).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite figure/panel numbers, page/paragraph, and, when possible, provide quotations or screenshots so other readers can quickly locate the issue. Vague remarks (‘this paper is wrong’) are discouraged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support assertions with evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Substantiate critiques with data, calculations, references, links, or other concrete evidence rather than unsupported claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attach or link to primary sources, underlying datasets, code, re-analyses, or independent replication attempts where available. Explain the method you used to check or reanalyze results. Evidence-based comments are more useful and more likely to remain on the site.

rubrics_metrics.name: Constructive and professional tone
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments should be professional, civil, and focused on the science rather than on the authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid ad hominem language, insults, sarcasm, or inflammatory rhetoric. Frame observations as critiques of work and evidence, and suggest paths to clarify, correct, or replicate results when feasible.

rubrics_metrics.name: No personal attacks, harassment, or doxxing
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not post personal information about authors, nor attack them personally.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid naming private individuals beyond what is already public in the article or public records. Posting private contact information or other identifying material intended to harass is prohibited and subject to removal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid unsubstantiated allegations of misconduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Allegations of misconduct (e.g., fabrication, falsification) should not be made without supporting evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you suspect misconduct, present objective, documented evidence (image manipulation traces, inconsistent data, duplicated text) rather than speculation. Clearly label what is observed and what is inferred, and avoid inflammatory accusations without proof.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anonymity and identity verification options
rubrics_metrics.description: PubPeer permits anonymous comments but also offers ways to verify identity (e.g., via ORCID) for those who wish to sign their posts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anonymous posting is allowed to protect commenters, especially whistleblowers; however verified identities or signed comments may lend credibility. Choose anonymity conscientiously and be aware that moderation/legal processes may affect anonymous posts in some jurisdictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflicts of interest and disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclose any relevant conflicts of interest that could affect the interpretation of your comment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you have a personal, financial, or professional relationship with the authors, the topic, or the journal, state it in your comment to allow readers to weigh potential biases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Format comments to aid readability
rubrics_metrics.description: Use clear structure, numbered points, and visual aids when helpful (e.g., annotated images, quoted text blocks, links).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Short, well-organised comments are more accessible: begin with a concise summary of the issue, then present evidence and suggested interpretation. When discussing images, indicate exact panels and, if possible, paste annotated images or links to high-resolution files.

rubrics_metrics.name: Image and data manipulation reporting guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: When pointing out potential image manipulation or data irregularities, describe precisely what you observed and supply supporting evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show side-by-side comparisons, mark duplicated regions, describe methods used to detect manipulation (contrast stretching, flipping, duplication), and link to original high-quality images or supplementary files. Avoid speculative phrasing unless explicitly flagged as hypothesis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Link to corrections, retractions, replications, and external resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Where relevant, link to journal corrections, errata, retraction notices, replication studies, or other external material that contextualises the comment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Providing these links helps readers evaluate the significance of the comment and track the post-publication record. If a journal has issued a correction, reference it and note whether the correction addresses the issue you raised.

rubrics_metrics.name: Moderation and removal criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments may be moderated or removed if they violate site rules (spam, off-topic content, personal attacks, illegal content, doxxing, defamatory statements without evidence).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Moderators apply policies intended to keep discussions focused and lawful. If a comment is removed, the author may be informed of the reason and, where appropriate, given guidance for revision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal considerations and takedown policy
rubrics_metrics.description: The platform complies with applicable law; defamatory or illegal content may be removed or subject to legal requests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid publishing content that could be libelous or that reveals private personal information. If you are unsure whether content crosses legal lines, focus on objective evidence and avoid accusatory language.

rubrics_metrics.name: When to contact journals or institutions
rubrics_metrics.description: PubPeer is for public scientific discussion; certain serious issues (e.g., clear evidence of fraud, safety concerns) may also warrant contacting the journal/editor or an institutional body.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you have direct evidence of misconduct or concerns about subject safety, consider alerting the journal editors or institutional officials in parallel with or instead of a public comment, following appropriate channels and preserving evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respect for privacy and sensitive material
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not post patient-identifying information or other sensitive data that should remain private.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Redact or avoid disclosing any personally identifiable or sensitive data in comments. Instead, describe issues at the level of the published material without reproducing private details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encouragement to improve reproducibility and transparency
rubrics_metrics.description: Use comments to request or point to additional methodological detail, code, raw data, or materials that would improve reproducibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suggest specific files or methods the authors could make available, and, where possible, provide re-analysis code or steps so others can reproduce your checks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expectations for civil engagement and community norms
rubrics_metrics.description: The community is expected to engage civilly, correct mistakes, and update comments if new information appears.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be willing to update or retract your comment if subsequent evidence resolves the issue. If authors respond, engage constructively rather than escalating.
